scenarios.purpose: Inert prose runs nothing: the unaffected control for every selection change.
A lane-root crate nothing else depends on reaches its own artifact and consumers, and no provider or editor lane.
The language server reaches editor and provider lanes, and no wasm lane.
An extension source runs the JavaScript and editor lanes behind its native artifact, and no Rust lane.
Reverse-dependent closure has a direction: the engine's dependents include the session; the session's do not include the engine.
A crate no lane root depends on runs only the crate-wide lanes.
A build script belongs to its crate, so its closure is the crate's closure.
A proc macro changes how its dependents compile, so it selects every impact-bearing lane.
A shared test helper reaches its dependents through dev-dependency edges.
A feature-bearing manifest keeps its crate's closure, and a runner excluded from the workspace still selects its isolated lane.
Generated and included inputs reach the lanes that read them, not only a Rust glob.
Each input that changes how every crate builds selects every impact-bearing lane; each array is a separate sample.
A change to what CI runs or how selection is made cannot exempt itself: every lane runs.
A path nobody classified fails closed: every lane runs rather than a guess.

Renames and deletions: a rename inside a crate is that crate's change; a deleted crate reaches every impact-bearing lane through the workspace files its removal must change. The source-only sample records the closure the current graph cannot see, because a deleted crate is not in the new metadata.
Interacting parents: two changes together select at least what each selects alone.
Release events: a release pull request keeps its lanes and names its kind; its landed commit runs none because the pull request's CI tested that tree.
Missed normal edge: an impact graph without the wasm root's dependencies must not satisfy the wasm lane's obligation.
Missed dev edge: an impact graph without dev-dependencies must not satisfy a shared test helper's dependents.
Synthetic closure seeds: transitive reach, isolated crate, dev edge, and normal/build/dev edges in the reverse graph.

scenarios.purpose: A failing change every dependent inherits: a compile error at the bottom of the crate graph.
A failing test: the change compiles and its assertion fails.
A failing format lane: the change compiles and its tests pass, and only the format obligation can reject it.
A failing JavaScript test: the Rust lanes cannot reject this change.

streams.purpose: Three concurrent pull requests with superseded pushes: the newest heads progress without starvation and the unaffected pull request is not held back.
streams.expected: Every still-current head reaches a terminal disposition; superseded work stays in runner-minute totals and never counts as green, as a landing, or as zero latency.
streams.unavailableReason: needs hosted execution and an observable admission signal; the inventory records no public source-admission contract, so no local replay can substitute for this stream

streams.purpose: A superseded head's success arrives after the current head exists and must not prove it.

events.after: A1 proof held at the adapter's test barrier

streams.expected: A1's proof does not satisfy A3. FX08 is the local form of this rejection; a live adapter must replay it through its own barrier.
streams.unavailableReason: needs a controllable proof-delivery barrier in a live scheduler; none exists, so only the local FX08 fixtures answer this case

cells.purpose: Linux debug core suite, four shards over one nextest archive.
The archive producer; its cache state decides what its shards inherit.
No-debug-assertions and other build configurations; a debug pass does not answer these.
Feature-on instrumentation smoke; it never replaces a feature-off obligation.
Isolated compile-contract groups, each with its own feature set.
wasm32 artifact producer; a native pass is not a wasm result.
Debug LSP producer for the editor-neutral, VS Code and DX lanes.
Release LSP producer; debug and release LSP results are not interchangeable.
Release N-API producer behind the JavaScript and playground consumers.
The JavaScript workspace and the scripts' self-tests.
Windows, macOS and Linux native artifacts, reached only by a release event.
Per-platform release LSP binaries, reached only by a release event.
IDE-lane native artifacts, reached only by an IDE release event.

cacheConditions.definition: Observed restore miss for every Rust cache layer the cell's job declares, and every artifact the job consumes built by a producer that also missed.
Observed restore hit from a compatible successful producer on the same configuration, followed by the full required validation.
Any other combination of hits and misses across layers, reported layer by layer; never counted as cold or as warm.
Cache state neither controlled nor observed; retained as such and never inferred from elapsed time.
